title: Tech Note: Enhanced DOM Functions
author: David Adams
featured_technology: DOM XML commands (DOM GET XML ELEMENT VALUE/NAME, DOM Count XML attributes, DOM Get parent/first child XML element)
Custom error handling around invalid DOM node references

historical_commentary.text: This note packages a set of wrapper functions (DOM_GetElementValue, DOM_FindElementByName, DOM_AttributesToArrays, etc.) that harden 4D 2004's native DOM XML commands against invalid node references, crashes on certain attribute calls, and missing whitespace trimming — practical, defensive-programming patches for real gaps of the era. The specific bugs being worked around (e.g., a documented crash calling DOM Count XML attributes on the #document node) are almost certainly long fixed, and the whole DOM API surface is dated, but the underlying pattern of wrapping a fragile native API with safer, well-documented helper functions remains good practice today.
related_updates: 4D has since fixed many of the DOM XML command edge cases and crashes referenced in this era (e.g., issues with DOM Count XML attributes on #document nodes)
DOM/SAX XML commands remain in modern 4D but see far less use than JSON parsing for typical data interchange
